fixes.explanation: Battles sound like a heavy-hitter reason, so I get why this one tempts a baker. But David never mentions a single battle in this song. His reason is right there in the first verse: "For I have walked with integrity…" If it were me, I'd show up with a whole highlight reel.
Not quite, friend. David says, "Test me, O LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind." So his heart and mind are right there in the request, not left out. That's the part the card leaves off.
Right, it's false. David says, "Test me, O LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind." He doesn't leave his heart off the table. I think that takes nerve.

Yes, friend. David says, "For Your loving devotion is before my eyes, and I have walked in Your truth." What's before his eyes is the LORD's loving devotion. And in the same breath, he says he has walked in the LORD's truth.

That's it. David says, "I do not sit with deceitful men, nor keep company with hypocrites." Deceitful men come first, and hypocrites follow right behind them. Those are the two kinds of company he names.

Foolish men don't show up in this verse. David says, "I do not sit with deceitful men, nor keep company with hypocrites." Deceitful and hypocrites are the two he names. Foolish is a fine word, but it didn't make the list.

Yes, hates. David says, "I hate the mob of evildoers, and refuse to sit with the wicked." It's a strong word, and he puts it in the song plainly. His seat choice matches it: he refuses to sit with the wicked.
Leads doesn't fit what David says. He says, "I hate the mob of evildoers, and refuse to sit with the wicked." Hate and refusing to sit are his words, not leading. That's the word to catch.

Standing before the people sounds like a believable reason, but that isn't what David says. He says, "I wash my hands in innocence that I may go about Your altar, O LORD…" The altar is where his washing is headed.
A palace is a natural guess, but the text never mentions one in this song. He says, "O LORD, I love the house where You dwell, the place where Your glory resides." The love goes to the LORD's house.

Yes, that's the request. David says, "Do not take my soul away with sinners, or my life with men of bloodshed…" Then he describes those men: wicked schemes in their hands, and bribes in their right hands. That's the company he doesn't want to be taken away with.

Hiding His face is a different prayer, and it's not in this song. Here David says, "Do not take my soul away with sinners, or my life with men of bloodshed…" His request is about being taken away with sinners.

This one is true, actually. David describes the men of bloodshed as those "in whose hands are wicked schemes, whose right hands are full of bribes." So wicked schemes are in their hands, just as the card says. It's a picture of hands full of the wrong things.

Yes, bless. David closes with, "My feet stand on level ground; in the congregations I will bless the LORD." The song opens with David asking to be vindicated and ends with him blessing the LORD. He plans to do it in the congregations, with other people around.
